raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- AMD ships AVX512-FP16 from 6th Gen EPYC (Venice) onwards, so make the dtype list reflect what the part can actually do instead of assuming no Zen CPU can.

- `float16` is accepted on Zen CPUs that report AVX512-FP16, and still rejected (auto-downcast to `bfloat16`) on Turin and earlier. No behavior change on any currently-shipping part.

- Bumps the zentorch pin from `2.13.0.1` to `2.14.0.1` in `setup.py` and the matching Buildkite `ZENTORCH_VERSION`. [2.14.0.1](https://pypi.org/project/zentorch/2.14.0.1/) is the release whose notes read *"functional support for running LLMs using float16 precision with vLLM on 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors"*.

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [CPU][Zen] Update zentorch to 2.14.0.1 & enable float16 on Venice and later

detail.body:
- AMD ships AVX512-FP16 from 6th Gen EPYC (Venice) onwards, so make the dtype list reflect what the part can actually do instead of assuming no Zen CPU can.

- `float16` is accepted on Zen CPUs that report AVX512-FP16, and still rejected (auto-downcast to `bfloat16`) on Turin and earlier. No behavior change on any currently-shipping part.

- Bumps the zentorch pin from `2.13.0.1` to `2.14.0.1` in `setup.py` and the matching Buildkite `ZENTORCH_VERSION`. [2.14.0.1](https://pypi.org/project/zentorch/2.14.0.1/) is the release whose notes read *"functional support for running LLMs using float16 precision with vLLM on 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors"*.
detail.title: [CPU][Zen] Update zentorch to 2.14.0.1 & enable float16 on Venice and later

files.patch:
@@ -277,7 +277,7 @@ steps:
     # `uv pip install "vllm[zen]"`, which forces uv to re-resolve vLLM's full
     # dependency closure and chokes on its transitive triton-cpu URL dependency.
     # Keep this pin in sync with the `zen` extra in setup.py.
-    ZENTORCH_VERSION: "2.13.0.1"
+    ZENTORCH_VERSION: "2.14.0.1"
   retry:
     automatic:
       - exit_status: 1  # Transient Docker/BuildKit failure

@@ -159,7 +159,7 @@ VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT=cpu VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu
 ### Which `dtype` should be used?
 
 - Currently, vLLM CPU uses model default settings as `dtype`. However, due to unstable float16 support in torch CPU, it is recommended to explicitly set `dtype=bfloat16` if there are any performance or accuracy problem.  
-- On AMD Zen CPUs (`ZenCpuPlatform`), `float16` is **not** supported. Only `bfloat16` and `float32` are accepted; models declared with `float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at model load time. See [AMD Zen optimizations](#amd-zen-optimizations).
+- On AMD Zen CPUs (`ZenCpuPlatform`), `float16` requires AVX512-FP16, available from Venice (6th Gen EPYC) onwards. On Turin (5th Gen EPYC) and earlier only `bfloat16` and `float32` are accepted, and models declared with `float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at model load time. See [AMD Zen optimizations](#amd-zen-optimizations).
 
 ### How to launch a vLLM service on CPU?

@@ -273,7 +273,9 @@ Otherwise, vLLM falls back to the default `CpuPlatform` (oneDNN / sgl-kernel pat
 
 ### Supported dtypes
 
-`float16` is **not** supported on `ZenCpuPlatform`. `ZenCpuPlatform.supported_dtypes` advertises only `bfloat16` and `float32`, so models declared with `torch_dtype=float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at load time with the standard `"Your device 'cpu' doesn't support torch.float16. Falling back to torch.bfloat16 for compatibility."` warning emitted from `vllm/config/model.py`.
+`ZenCpuPlatform.supported_dtypes` always advertises `bfloat16` and `float32`, and adds `float16` when `torch.ops.zentorch.zentorch_is_fp16_supported()` reports AVX512-FP16, which AMD ships from Venice (6th Gen EPYC) onwards. On Turin (5th Gen EPYC) and earlier, models declared with `torch_dtype=float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at load time with the standard `"Your device 'cpu' doesn't support torch.float16. Falling back to torch.bfloat16 for compatibility."` warning emitted from `vllm/config/model.py`.
+
+`bfloat16` is listed first either way, so `--dtype auto` keeps resolving to it.
 
 ### Environment variables

@@ -1688,7 +1688,7 @@ def add_vllm_package_data(filename: str) -> None:
     install_requires=get_requirements(),
     extras_require={
         # AMD Zen CPU optimizations via zentorch
-        "zen": ["zentorch==2.14.0.0"],
+        "zen": ["zentorch==2.14.0.1"],
         "bench": ["pandas", "matplotlib", "seaborn", "datasets", "scipy", "plotly"],
         "tensorizer": ["tensorizer==2.10.1"],
         "fastsafetensors": ["fastsafetensors >= 0.3.3"],

@@ -2,9 +2,11 @@
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 import builtins
 import logging
+from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest.mock import mock_open, patch
 
 import pytest
+import torch
 
 from vllm.platforms import (
     _is_amd_zen_cpu,
@@ -139,3 +141,18 @@ def failing_plugin():
     assert platform == "vllm.platforms.interface.UnspecifiedPlatform"
     assert "Platform plugin cpu failed during detection" in caplog_vllm.text
     assert "RuntimeError: plugin exploded" in caplog_vllm.text
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fp16_supported", [True, False])
+def test_zen_cpu_supported_dtypes_track_fp16_capability(fp16_supported):
+    from vllm.platforms.zen_cpu import ZenCpuPlatform
+
+    # zentorch is absent on most CI hosts, so torch.ops.zentorch has to be
+    # stood up rather than patched in place.
+    zentorch_ops = SimpleNamespace(zentorch_is_fp16_supported=lambda: fp16_supported)
+    with patch.object(torch.ops, "zentorch", zentorch_ops, create=True):
+        dtypes = ZenCpuPlatform().supported_dtypes
+
+    # bf16 stays first so `--dtype auto` resolves to it on every Zen part.
+    assert dtypes[0] is torch.bfloat16
+    assert (torch.float16 in dtypes) is fp16_supported

@@ -25,8 +25,10 @@ def is_zen_cpu(self) -> bool:
         # is_cpu() also returns True for this platform (inherited from CpuPlatform).
         return True
 
-    # Currently, AMD CPUs do not support float16 compute.
-    # Hence explicitly return bfloat16 and float32.
+    # fp16 compute needs AVX512-FP16, which AMD ships from Venice (6th Gen
+    # EPYC) onwards; Turin (5th Gen EPYC) and earlier have no fp16 kernels.
     @property
     def supported_dtypes(self) -> list[torch.dtype]:
+        if torch.ops.zentorch.zentorch_is_fp16_supported():
+            return [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float16]
         return [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32]
